157	not the socket protocol), `needsDesignRound: true` per the multi-area rule, `engineModel: sonnet`
158	(each test maps to a named file and a "passes on clean dev" done-check), `planModel: opus-4.8`
159	(the spec enumerates every failure and its error text).
160	Consequences: test-only fixes that need a `multiplayer_server/scripts/*` sim rewritten still get
161	the short multi-area design round; the plan should say explicitly that no renderer or relay code
162	changes and that the sim moves to the `_setForTest` fixture pattern rather than re-stubbing fetch.

373	Context: card "When I enter the website it takes a long time to see that I am actually logged
374	in" (fullstack, Difficulty override `hard`, title-only spec). Root cause is a post-hydration
375	waterfall in `src/app/providers.tsx` `checkLogin`: Redux starts logged-out, and with a 15-minute
376	access token nearly every return visit does `/me/` (401) → `token/refresh/` (rotation + blacklist
377	write) → `/me/` again, three sequential hops to a cold Vercel serverless Django + Supabase pooler,
378	while `Navigation`/`Landpage` render the guest UI until the last one resolves. Fable was
379	defensible: the fix touches token/session code on the AUTH-9 `risk: high` list, and there are real
380	subtleties — a localStorage read during render is a Next hydration mismatch (must be an effect or
381	a pre-hydration inline script), an optimistic cached user must reconcile without a logout flash,
382	and skipping the dead `/me/` hop means decoding `exp` client-side.
383	Decision: `engineModel: sonnet`, `planModel: fable` (thin spec). The design round can name every
384	mechanism up front — cache the last `/me/` payload under a fixed localStorage key, hydrate the
385	slice optimistically in the mount effect when a refresh token exists, proactively refresh when the
386	access token is expired instead of eating a 401, reconcile with `/me/` in the background, and
387	optionally have `SessionRefreshView` return `user` so it is one hop — each with a done-check.

## 2026-09-29 — "Copy link" button next to the room code: frontend-only standard vs multi-area hard
Context: card "Add a 'copy link' button next to the room code" (Category frontend, one-line spec).
`FriendPlay.tsx` already has a copy-code button (`copy-to-clipboard`, `copied` state) in
`.fp-code-row`, but no join link exists anywhere: nothing in `src/` reads a room/code query param.
So the card really means two things: a second copy button, and deep-link handling. When a
`?room=<6 digits>` URL is opened on the game page, it must open the friend flow and call the existing
`joinFriendRoom`. The alternative was `areas` + `multiplayer`, `hard`, and a design round, because
it touches the friend-room join flow in `MultiplayerContext`.
Decision: `standard`, `areas: ["frontend","ui"]`, `risk: low`, sonnet, no design round. The client
already exposes `joinFriendRoom(code)`, the socket protocol and `multiplayer_server/` stay untouched,
and the work is a bounded pattern: build the URL from `window.location` plus the code, copy it
with the existing helper, and on mount read the param, switch to the friend flow, join, then strip
the param. `MULTIPLAYER_CONSTRAINTS.md` is still in `docs` for the join-flow rules.
Consequences: client-only additions that reuse existing `MultiplayerContext` actions stay
frontend/standard. Once a change needs a new socket event or relay change, it is `multiplayer`,
`hard`, `risk: high`. The engine must handle the logged-out and already-in-a-room cases for a deep
link, and must read the search param in a client effect so SSR stays hydration-safe.
